title: Zuriel Chapter Introductions — 2 Chronicles 1–18 (Part 1)
description: Chapter-by-chapter study of Judah's kings, temple worship, reform, prophetic truth, exile, and the hope of return.

chapters.title: 2 Chronicles 1 — Solomon asks for wisdom
chapters.historicalContext: Solomon seeks wisdom to govern, receives God's favour, and establishes the kingdom.
chapters.overview: Solomon seeks wisdom to govern, receives God's favour, and establishes the kingdom.
chapters.studyObservation: Observe how worship, leadership, prophetic truth, public justice, and the choices of kings shape the Chronicler's account of Judah.
chapters.connectionNotes: Read 2 Chronicles 1–2 as a connected unit. Compare parallel passages in Kings and Samuel, noticing the Chronicler's particular attention to temple worship, reform, and the returned community.
studyQuestions: What decisions and events shape this chapter?
How does the account connect leadership, worship, justice, and covenant faithfulness?
Which details are emphasized, and what assumptions should readers avoid?
chapters.lifeApplication: Consider faithful worship, humility, truthful counsel, justice, repentance, and responsibility. Apply enduring principles thoughtfully without copying ancient royal actions or assuming every historical outcome has a direct modern equivalent.
chapters.interpretiveCaution: Royal histories are theological narratives, not simplistic formulas that every success proves divine approval or every hardship proves personal wrongdoing. Distinguish the narrator's evaluation from assumptions about modern events.
chapters.readingNote: Read with the wider biblical story and compare parallel accounts carefully; the Chronicler writes with a distinct theological perspective.
